notes: Perfect claim overlap (C8, C77-C81) regarding adult fly function. Both evaluations agree evidence is insufficient: LLM notes 'preliminary and limited' data with only one bacterial species tested; peer reviewers state 'effect has been seen only in early embryos' and request discussion of adult organism applicability.

Near-perfect overlap (11/12 claims: C2, C3, C83-C89, C105, C121) on LPS/LTA-triggered histone release mechanism. Both find evidence convincing: LLM describes 'dose-dependent release clearly demonstrated by Western blot'; peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'remarkable new finding' without challenge.

Strong overlap (19 shared claims) covering core embryo infection findings including Jabba mutant phenotypes and bacterial survival data. Both strongly support: LLM cites 'two independent alleles, >4-fold survival advantage across four bacterial species'; peer reviewers call it 'outstanding' with 'large difference in bacterial growth' and 'four to five fold difference in embryo survival.'

Moderate overlap (6 shared claims: C9, C93-C97) on mammalian conservation. Both find evidence insufficient: LLM states 'preliminary data' with 'no functional experiments performed'; peer reviewers note 'experiments presented are rather limited' and recommend to 'tone down this section,' suggesting bacterial killing assays would strengthen claims.

Partial overlap (6 shared claims: C1, C33-C35, C43-C44) on antibacterial activity of purified lipid droplets and histone identification. Both support the findings: LLM emphasizes 'multiple independent assays' and 'convergence of experimental approaches'; peer reviewers describe 'remarkable new finding' with 'outstanding results.'

Minimal overlap (4 shared claims: C53, C54, C56, C137) touching on Jabba mutant genetic evidence. LLM finds genetic evidence SUPPORTED by 'two independently derived alleles with similar phenotypes'; peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, recommending 'Jabba be tested in another mutant background (jabba/deficiency) to exclude possible background effect.'

LLM evaluates electrostatic binding mechanism and histone PTM characterization (C36, C45-C49, C126-C127). No corresponding peer review result addresses these specific mechanistic claims about binding chemistry. LLM finds carbonate wash and mass spec data supportive.

LLM evaluates overall model of lipid droplet defense function (C100, C108, C109, C116). No direct peer review result addresses this synthetic/conceptual claim set. LLM finds model well-supported by convergence of evidence across multiple experimental systems.
